headline: ASK demands impartial probe into journalist's killing in Netrokona
summary: Human rights organization Ain and Salish Kendra (ASK) has called for the immediate identification and prosecution of those responsible for the murder of Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir.
details: Human rights organization Ain and Salish Kendra (ASK) has expressed deep concern and strong condemnation over the shooting death of journalist Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir in Netrokona's Durgapur.
Alif Fakir, a representative for the private IPTV channel Ruposhi Bangla, was shot dead on the night of October 15 in the Telanjia area of Durgapur.
ASK highlighted that Alif had previously been attacked in November 2025, raising concerns over the failure to ensure his safety after the initial assault.
The organization stated that killing a journalist is not only an attack on a single life but a dangerous message to independent journalism, freedom of expression, and the public's right to know.

ASK emphasized that the state has a constitutional duty to protect journalists and ensure effective investigation and justice for any violence against them, citing Articles 32 and 39 of the Bangladesh Constitution.
Executive Director of ASK, Tahmina Rahman, stated that there should be no negligence, influence, or bias in the investigation of this killing.
The organization urged authorities to quickly identify and bring all involved parties to justice to ensure a safe environment where journalists can perform their professional duties without threats.
caption:
A journalist was shot dead in Netrokona, and now human rights advocates are demanding justice. Why was he not protected after a previous attack?

Human rights organization Ain and Salish Kendra (ASK) has expressed deep concern and strong condemnation over the shooting death of journalist Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir in Netrokona's Durgapur.

Alif Fakir, a representative for the private IPTV channel Ruposhi Bangla, was shot dead on the night of October 15 in the Telanjia area of Durgapur.

ASK highlighted that Alif had previously been attacked in November 2025, raising concerns over the failure to ensure his safety after the initial assault.

The organization stated that killing a journalist is not only an attack on a single life but a dangerous message to independent journalism, freedom of expression, and the public's right to know.

ASK emphasized that the state has a constitutional duty to protect journalists and ensure effective investigation and justice for any violence against them, citing Articles 32 and 39 of the Bangladesh Constitution.

Executive Director of ASK, Tahmina Rahman, stated that there should be no negligence, influence, or bias in the investigation of this killing.

The organization urged authorities to quickly identify and bring all involved parties to justice to ensure a safe environment where journalists can perform their professional duties without threats.

#Bangladesh #Journalism #PressFreedom #Netrokona #HumanRights #Justice

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune

headline: Man with 14 criminal cases shot dead in Rajbari
summary: Piarul Sardar, 32, was killed by motorcycle-borne gunmen in Sajnokanda, Rajbari’s Sadar upazila, on Friday evening.
details: Piarul Sardar, 32, was shot dead on Friday evening at Sajnokanda in Rajbari’s Sadar upazila.
According to Rajbari SP Mir Monir Hossain, Piarul was standing about 200 metres from his house around 6:45 pm when two men on a motorcycle arrived and fired two shots at him.
Locals rushed to the spot and took him to Rajbari Sadar Hospital, where he was later referred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital, but he died on the way.
District police are currently collecting CCTV footage to identify the perpetrators, and several police teams are working on the case.
SP Monir also revealed that Piarul was an accused in 13 to 14 criminal cases, including those involving drugs, arms, and murder.
caption:
